title: Highest temperature in London on September 2?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent Met Office guidance and supporting model runs point to a mostly cloudy Wednesday in London with light morning rain possible before turning drier, limiting daytime heating under southwest breezes and producing a maximum near 21–23 °C.** 

This range aligns with the market’s heaviest weighting on 21 °C (38.5 %) and 22 °C (27.5 %), followed by 20 °C (23.0 %). Persistent cloud cover reduces incoming solar radiation while moderate winds enhance mixing, preventing the urban heat-island effect from pushing readings much above the mid-20s. Ensemble spreads remain modest only 24–36 hours ahead, but slight differences in rain timing and low-level moisture explain why 23 °C carries just 5.5 % and warmer outcomes are near zero. 

Traders are therefore pricing the highest temperature around the lower end of official guidance, reflecting both the current synoptic pattern and the narrow window before resolution.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current short-range forecasts from AEMET and global models position Madrid's September 2 maximum near 35–36 °C, driving the market's strong 63.5 % weighting on 36 °C. Final official readings from Madrid–Retiro or Barajas will resolve the market once the daily maximum is confirmed.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Typhoon No. 18's outer circulation is the dominant near-term driver**, delivering increased cloud cover, scattered showers or thunderstorms, and easterly flow that limits insolation and caps daytime heating across northern Taiwan. Official Central Weather Administration guidance for Taipei on September 2 projects a high of 33–34 °C under predominantly cloudy conditions with a 20–40 % chance of brief rain, consistent with climatological September norms of 30–32 °C. Model spreads arise mainly from the timing and intensity of convective cells: clearer afternoon breaks could briefly push readings to 35 °C, while sustained low-level moisture and rain-cooled air favor a peak near 33 °C. High humidity will elevate apparent temperature (35–36 °C), but the market resolves on dry-bulb maximum. Updated model runs and CWA afternoon briefings tomorrow morning remain the key catalysts for any late shifts in trader positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus positions 21°C as the clear frontrunner for Amsterdam’s September 2 maximum temperature.** Multiple models, including GFS-based outputs, indicate a high near 20–22°C (roughly 68–72°F) under mostly cloudy skies with southwest winds of 10–14 mph and modest humidity. This aligns with the long-term average high of 20.8°C for the date and produces the market’s heavy weighting toward 21°C (51.5%) and 22°C (37.5%).

Key atmospheric drivers include persistent cloud cover that limits daytime heating and a mild maritime flow that prevents significant warming or cooling. No strong frontal passages or clear-sky radiative heating are expected to push temperatures outside the narrow 20–22°C band. Recent model runs have remained stable, with only minor adjustments to cloud timing that have not shifted the overall temperature envelope.

Traders therefore price the outcome as a low-uncertainty, high-consensus event typical of short-range European weather markets, where official guidance and ensemble agreement tightly constrain the probable range.

Early September sits in the core of the rainy season, when frequent afternoon convection, cloud cover, and widespread moisture limit insolation and cap daytime peaks. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus for Zhengzhou on September 2 centers on a high near 30°C under mostly clear skies and light northeast winds.** Multiple sources, including WeatherBug (87°F/30.6°C), Yr.no (30°C), and WindBorne (86°F/30°C), indicate sunny to mostly sunny conditions with minimal cloud cover and negligible precipitation risk.
